If external torque is zero ($\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0$), angular momentum is conserved ($I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$). Rotational kinetic energy $K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.
concepts.standard_formulas: \tau = I\alpha, \quad L = I\omega, \quad K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2, \quad I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2
concepts.common_traps: When a ballet dancer pulls in her arms, $I$ decreases, $\omega$ increases, but rotational kinetic energy INCREASES due to internal muscular work done!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Convert rpm to rad/s: $\omega = \frac{2\pi N}{60}$. A common 1-step calculation in KCET rotational problems.

concepts.summary: Moment of inertia $I = \sum m_i r_i^2 = M k^2$. Parallel axis theorem: $I = I_{cm} + M d^2$. Perpendicular axis theorem for laminar bodies: $I_z = I_x + I_y$. Standard values: Ring about axis $M R^2$; Disc $\frac{1}{2}M R^2$; Solid Sphere $\frac{2}{5}M R^2$; Thin Rod $\frac{1}{12}M L^2$.
concepts.standard_formulas: I_{\text{disc}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2, \quad I_{\text{solid sphere}} = \frac{2}{5}MR^2, \quad I_{\text{tangent}} = I_{cm} + Md^2
concepts.common_traps: Perpendicular axis theorem applies ONLY to flat planar (2D) lamina, NEVER to 3D objects like solid spheres or cylinders!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: For rolling bodies down an incline, acceleration is $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + k^2/r^2}$. Smaller $k^2/r^2$ reaches bottom first: Solid Sphere ($0.4$) > Disc ($0.5$) > Ring ($1.0$).

### 2.1 Torque, Angular Momentum & Rotational Kinetic Energy (Rotational Dynamics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **7 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Rotational dynamics: Torque $\tau = I\alpha = \frac{dL}{dt}$. Angular momentum $L = I\omega = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$. If external torque is zero ($\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0$), angular momentum is conserved ($I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$). Rotational kinetic energy $K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\tau = I\alpha, \quad L = I\omega, \quad K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2, \quad I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: When a ballet dancer pulls in her arms, $I$ decreases, $\omega$ increases, but rotational kinetic energy INCREASES due to internal muscular work done!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Convert rpm to rad/s: $\omega = \frac{2\pi N}{60}$. A common 1-step calculation in KCET rotational problems.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"If the earth were to suddenly contract to half of its present radius, what would be the duration of the day?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2026 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"The angular momentum of a moving body remains constant, if..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2025 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Two fly wheels are connected by a non-slipping belt as shown in the figure. $I_{1}=4kgm^{2},r_{1}=20cm$ , $I_{2}=20kgm^{2}$ and $r_{2}=30cm$..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"A body of mass 1 kg is suspended by a weightless string which passes over a frictionless pulley of mass 2 kg as shown in the figure. The mas..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Moment of Inertia & Theorems of Parallel / Perpendicular Axes (Rotational Inertia)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **6 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Moment of inertia $I = \sum m_i r_i^2 = M k^2$. Parallel axis theorem: $I = I_{cm} + M d^2$. Perpendicular axis theorem for laminar bodies: $I_z = I_x + I_y$. Standard values: Ring about axis $M R^2$; Disc $\frac{1}{2}M R^2$; Solid Sphere $\frac{2}{5}M R^2$; Thin Rod $\frac{1}{12}M L^2$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
I_{\text{disc}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2, \quad I_{\text{solid sphere}} = \frac{2}{5}MR^2, \quad I_{\text{tangent}} = I_{cm} + Md^2
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Perpendicular axis theorem applies ONLY to flat planar (2D) lamina, NEVER to 3D objects like solid spheres or cylinders!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: For rolling bodies down an incline, acceleration is $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + k^2/r^2}$. Smaller $k^2/r^2$ reaches bottom first: Solid Sphere ($0.4$) > Disc ($0.5$) > Ring ($1.0$).

- **[2023 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Seven identical discs are arranged in a planar pattern, so as to touch each other as shown in the figure. Each disc has mass $m$ radius $R$ ..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Rotational Motion

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
